faqs.q: How much does a doula cost in Saint Petersburg, FL?
faqs.a: In Saint Petersburg and the surrounding Tampa Bay area, birth doula services typically range from $650 to $1,800. Packages may include prenatal visits, continuous labor support, and a postpartum follow-up. Some families qualify for free doula services through the Healthy Start Coalition of Pinellas.

faqs.q: Does Florida Medicaid cover doula services?
faqs.a: As of 2025, Florida Medicaid covers maternity care through Managed Medical Assistance plans, but doula services may not be directly covered. The Healthy Start Coalition of Pinellas offers a free doula program for eligible Pinellas County residents. Private doulas often provide superbills for HSA/FSA reimbursement.

faqs.q: What hospitals deliver babies in Saint Petersburg?
faqs.a: Orlando Health Bayfront Hospital (adjacent to Johns Hopkins All Children's Hospital NICU) and HCA Florida St. Petersburg Hospital are the two main hospitals serving Saint Petersburg families. Both offer private L&D rooms, lactation support, and welcome doulas.

faqs.q: Is there a birth center near Saint Petersburg?
faqs.a: Breath of Life Women's Health & Birth Center in Largo (~6 miles from Saint Petersburg) is Florida's only CABC-accredited birth center, offering midwife-led care, water birth, and a home transfer plan.

faqs.q: Can I have a water birth in Saint Petersburg?
faqs.a: Water birth is available at Breath of Life Women's Health & Birth Center in Largo. Most hospitals in the area offer labor tubs, but routine water birth may not be available. Ask your provider about water labor options.

faqs.q: How do I choose a doula in Saint Petersburg?
faqs.a: Start by reviewing certifications, services offered, and whether they serve Pinellas County. Schedule consultations with 2–3 doulas to find someone whose approach matches your birth plan. Consider Pinellas Doula Services, Quantum Motherhood, or the free Healthy Start Coalition program.
